title: Segmented On‑Prem Activation Guide — TF slimline notes (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a working draft for a compact, repeatable activation/playbook for segmented on-prem VPC deployments. Focus is on tenant isolation (per-tenant subnets + policy), minimal TF surface for customers, and a safe upgrade path for existing greenfield/brownfield sites. Target audience: solutions engineers, field SRE, and delivery engs performing the first 3 customer activations for the new 'segmented tenant' pattern.

High-level goals:
- Provide a small set of Terraform modules and a deployment sequence that is idempotent and auditable.
- Keep customer-facing surface minimal: two main manifests (network bootstrap + control-plane bootstrap).
- Ensure predictable rollback and non-disruptive patch/upgrade windows.
- Capture common on-prem gotchas (MTU, DNS, BGP flaps, local firewall defaults).

Assumptions (customer and Redwood):
- Customer provides a transit VLAN and at least one /22 CIDR for tenant subnet allocation, or agrees to use RFC1918 private pool managed by Redwood operator.
- KMS/HSM integration is negotiated (if required) before install window.
- On-prem hypervisor or k8s cluster is >= K8s 1.25 (we default to kubeadm installs for the first pass).
- Remote state will live in customer-controlled S3-compatible object store with locking via DynamoDB-style or Consul (we support both patterns).

Reference logical layout (text diagram):
- Management VLAN (10.100.0.0/24): provisioning hosts, jump boxes, remote-state endpoint
- Transit VLAN (10.101.0.0/24): BGP peer to customer router (if available) or static NAT/edge box
- Tenant pool (10.128.0.0/18): subdivided into per-tenant /24s allocated by operator
- Control-plane subnet (10.200.0.0/24): internal services, metrics, config-sync

Key operators/components to deploy (sequence):
1) network-bootstrap (TF): creates subnets, route tables, initial ACLs, and tenant CIDR allocation table (CRD for operator).
2) edge-proxy (container): a lightweight NAT/egress appliance for controlled egress and local caching.
3) tenant-operator (K8s): responsible for allocating per-tenant namespaces, network policies, and injecting per-tenant routing rules.
4) control-plane services: redis, db (if local), metrics collector, certificate manager (cert-manager), and optional local HSM connector.

Terraform module notes (slimline):
- modules/network-bootstrap: inputs: tenant_cidr_pool (string), management_vlan_id (string), transit_vlan_id (string), edge_asn (int, optional), enable_bgp (bool, default false), dns_split_zones (map). Outputs: control_plane_subnet, tenant_allocation_table_id, state_lock_resource.
- modules/egress-nat: inputs: egress_nodes (list[string]), nat_ip_pool (list[string] or cidr), health_check_url, enable_snat_by_tenant (bool). Side note: prefer SNAT at egress device for onprem — easier rollback.
- modules/remote-state: supports backend: s3-compatible|gcs|azblob, lock: dynamodb|consul, tf_version (string). Dev note: keep remote-state module minimal in customer repo and reference canonical module via git tag.

Idempotency and state partitioning guidance:
- Partition remote state per-customer and per-environment (customerX-network.tfstate, customerX-controlplane.tfstate).
- Avoid cross-module implicit dependencies: use explicit outputs (e.g., control_plane_subnet) not data lookups in separate state files.
- When upgrading modules, follow this flow: bump module tag -> run plan in staging copy of customer state -> run plan with --target for critical resources first (route tables, ACLs) -> full apply.

Activation checklist (pre-week):
- Confirm customer VLANs and MTU (default 1500; any jumbo frames must be documented).
- Exchange BGP ASN and peering point if using dynamic routing.
- Confirm remote-state S3 endpoint + lock mechanism.
- Exchange public keys for jumpbox and SRE admin accounts.
- Verify contact window for maintenance and rollback windows.

Activation day runbook (high level):
- T-60: run network-bootstrap apply in dry-run workspace (terraform plan) and capture plan file.
- T-30: apply network-bootstrap to create management & transit subnets. Validate with customer network team (ping, traceroute to edge).
- T-15: deploy edge-proxy in a canary mode (1 node) and test egress flows: outbound to known endpoints, DNS resolution, SNI passthrough.
- T0: deploy tenant-operator to a control-plane namespace. Create one sample tenant (/24) and validate: namespace created, network policy applied, tenant egress NAT shows in logs.
- T+30: run internal smoke e2e (token issuance, simple inference call to local model endpoint, metrics ingestion).

Upgrade plan (minor module bump, non-disruptive):
- Schedule 60-min maintenance window (prefer low traffic hours).
- Create staging copy of remote state (snapshot).
- Apply module bump first to non-critical resources (tagging, metadata).
- Canary: pick 1 tenant with least traffic; apply full plan scoped to tenant operator resources for that tenant. Monitor for 30m.
- Roll-forward: if canary healthy, expand to 10% tenants, then 50%, then 100%. Use rate-limited rollout in terraform via scripted loops (we have example in infra-tools).
- Rollback: use terraform state rollback from snapshot or revert module tag and apply. Critical: ensure tenant operator deletes not happen on partial apply — we should mark deletion_protection = true on tenant CRs during upgrade.

Rollback play (fast path):
- If control-plane unavailable: revert to snapshot of controlplane state (requires snapshot + restore process doc — see linked artifact).
- If network broken: announce emergency window, apply rollback plan that replaces modified route table entries with previous ones (we keep planfile diffs for a quick revert).

Acceptance criteria (post-activation):
- 99.9% control-plane readiness within SLA for 24h after activation.
- No customer-visible 5xx on API gateway for tenant traffic during activation.
- Token-level cost and latency metrics reported in Redwood Console for at least one tenant.
- Certs issued and validated by cert-manager; KMS integration tested with a signing roundtrip.

Common gotchas and mitigation notes:
- MTU mismatch: If customer network uses 9000 and onprem devices default 1500, VXLAN overlays will fragment. Ask for MTU confirmation early and prefer setting vxlan mtu to 1450 in TF.
- Split-horizon DNS: internal services must use stub zones; cert-manager ACME challenges fail if DNS not resolvable internally.
- Firewall defaults block kubelet health checks; request temporary rules for provisioning IPs.
- BGP flaps: provision short dampening timers on the customer side during activation to avoid route churn.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we require a default per-tenant egress ACL or opt-out model? (Priya to decide, ENG-2713)
- Validate HSM connector PKCS#11 compatibility matrix for 2 customers scheduled Q1.
- Add automated post-apply tests to infra-tools repo (Liam assigned).

Quick TF snippets (examples, not copy/paste production):
- tenant allocation variable: variable "tenant_cidr_pool" { type = string description = "CIDR for tenant allocations, e.g. 10.128.0.0/18" }
- example usage: module "network" { source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules.git//modules/network-bootstrap?ref=v0.7.1" tenant_cidr_pool = var.tenant_cidr_pool management_vlan_id = var.management_vlan }

Notes to delivery team (voice-of-customer):
- Offer a 2hr discovery call before any onprem kickoff — helps us surface MTU, routing, and compliance requirements early.
- Keep TF changes small and modular; customers prefer explicit reviewers from their network team.

Appendix: quick checklist for rollback readiness:
- Snapshot remote-state before apply (mandatory).
- Export current route table entries (JSON).
- Keep previous module tag hash in deployment notes.
- Ensure SRE has VPN access and jumpbox key.

If this draft looks OK, next steps: convert to canonical playbook page on Confluence, add an automated checklist for solutions-engineers, and create a tiny demo repo that wires the modules together with a CI check that runs terraform plan on sample inputs.

Last edited by: Ava Ramirez (notes inline).
